Applied.Outcome: Resolved with no reply: all eleven recommendations taken. Written into the plan under "Decided before the build".

Replies.Text:
Design, Step 2: The Threads in the Editor. Eleven decisions, each with my recommendation first. Resolve with no reply to take them all; reply with the numbers you want otherwise, and I apply the result under "Decided before the build".

1. A selection to an anchor. AnchorMap gains PlainRange( Map, From, To ), the plain characters inside a source span as { Start, End } (null when the span holds none), the reverse of SourceRange; and the making of { Text, Prefix, Suffix } from a plain range, which Render.SelectionAnchor does for the rendered DOM, moves into Render.AnchorOf( Plain, Start, End ) (the trim and the context as today), so both views build the same anchor. PlainRange is tested in node with the map's fixtures.

2. The buttons. A selection-buttons component (bindings: anchor, text, at) holding Copy, Comment or Re-anchor here, and Start a new Subplan, with the actions that html-view has today moved into it; html-view and edit-view compute the anchor, the text and the position and show it. One markup, one behaviour; the ids (#copy-button, #comment-button, #subplan-button) stay on the Read view's. Alternative: a second copy of the buttons in edit-view; two copies drift.

3. When the editor offers them. On a non-empty main selection, once the mouse is up or a keyboard selection rests; placed under the selection's end (coordsAtPos); hidden on any edit or a collapsed selection. Copy always, copying the text as it reads (the plain text from the map; Ctrl+C in the editor copies the source, marks and all). Comment and Start a new Subplan only while the text is the saved one (not dirty, not stale), as the edit preview did; in Source mode too.

4. The scroll to a passage. A thread-selected that did not come from a mousedown in the editor (the thread header's anchor words, a card, a search hit) scrolls the editor to the thread's mark, centred (EditorView.scrollIntoView), and flashes it. The flash: a flash effect on the anchor field adding a class to the mark for a second, the keyframes in edit-view.css. The Read view keeps its scroll.

5. The pending. html-view's main one settles State.Pending only when Read is the view shown; edit-view settles it when Edit is: Select selects, scrolls and flashes; Scroll { text } finds the text in the map's plain, scrolls to it and flashes a temporary mark; Compose starts a comment on the whole document.

6. Re-anchor. The hint moves from the read section into document-editor, above whichever view is shown; Re-anchor here among the editor's buttons posts the anchor as the Read view does and selects the thread.

7. New Comment and Ctrl+Shift+C are offered in the CodeMirror Edit view too (the button's ng-show and the key's When become "a plan open, not archived").

8. A click off a mark in the editor does not deselect the thread: a click there places the cursor. Escape deselects, as it does now.

9. A document (the Readme, the instructions): no marks, Copy alone, in both views.

10. Tests. Node: PlainRange against SourceRange over the fixtures, both ways. Browser, CodeMirror mode: a selection in the editor shows the three buttons; Comment opens the compose card with the anchor's words; Start a new Subplan opens the subplan form; Re-anchor here moves a thread; the header's anchor words scroll the editor until the mark's box is inside the scroller, and the flash class comes and goes; a waiting item's link flashes the passage; a dirty text offers Copy alone. The smoke: the buttons on a selection in the editor.

11. Out of this step: the Read view's removal in CodeMirror mode (Step 3).
